_comment: Bundahishn, trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880): ox-lament, Gayomart, Mashya and Mashyoi. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: The Ox's Lament and the Covenant Deferred

region.en: Earth of the original creation (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 原初創世之土（象徵性定位）

source.work: Bundahishn chs. III-IV (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880)

summary.en: When the primeval ox passes away, its soul Geush-urvan stands before it and cries to Auharmazd as much as a thousand men at one time: with whom is the guardianship of the creatures left by thee, when ruin has broken into the earth, and vegetation is withered, and water is troubled? Where is the man of whom it was said by thee thus: I will produce him, so that he may preach carefulness? And Auharmazd answers: you are made ill, O Goshurvan; if it were proper to produce that man in this earth at this time, the evil spirit would not have been oppressive in it.
summary.zh: 原牛死去之際，其靈「牛魂」立於牛前，如千人齊呼般向阿胡拉·馬茲達哭訴：「大地已被毀、草木凋零、水已污濁，你曾說要造一人來教人謹守正道——他在哪裡？」答曰：「牛魂啊，你受了苦；若此人該在此世此時降生，惡靈便不會如此肆虐了。」

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal text rendered as myth; the ox's protest is Yasna 29's Geush Urvan. Cross-tradition: dismembered-giant cluster (Ymir/Purusha). No living community restriction.

passages.text: This also is said, that when the primeval ox passed away it fell to the right hand, and Gayomart afterwards, when he passed away, to the left hand. Goshurvan, as the soul of the primeval ox came out from the body of the ox, stood up before the ox and cried to Auharmazd, as much as a thousand men when they sustain a cry at one time, thus: with whom is the guardianship of the creatures left by thee, when ruin has broken into the earth, and vegetation is withered, and water is troubled? Where is the man of whom it was said by thee thus: I will produce him, so that he may preach carefulness?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. IV, 1-2 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

passages.text: And Auharmazd spoke thus: you are made ill, O Goshurvan; you have the illness which the evil spirit brought on; if it were proper to produce that man in this earth at this time, the evil spirit would not have been oppressive in it. And before his coming to the ox, Auharmazd ground up the healing fruit, small, in water openly before its eyes, so that its damage and discomfort from the calamity might be less; and when it became at the same time lean and ill, as its breath went forth and it passed away, the ox also spoke thus: the cattle are to be created, and their work, labour, and care are to be appointed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn chs. III 18, IV 3 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

title.en: Gayomart, the First Man, Born of Sweat
title.zh: 原人伽堯馬特誕於汗珠

region.en: Centre of the earth, Khvaniras (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 大地中央赫瓦尼拉斯（象徵性定位）

source.work: Bundahishn ch. III, 19-27 (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880)

summary.en: Before the destroyer's coming to Gayomart, Auharmazd brought forth a sweat upon Gayomart, so long as he might recite a prayer of one stanza; moreover he formed that sweat into the youthful body of a man of fifteen years, radiant and tall. When Gayomart issued from the sweat he saw the world dark as night, and the earth as though not a needle's point remained free from noxious creatures; and though Asto-vidad with a thousand demons was let forth on him, his appointed time had not come: after the coming of the adversary he lived thirty years, and spoke: although the destroyer has come, mankind will be all of my race.
summary.zh: 毀滅者來襲之前，阿胡拉·馬茲達使原人伽堯馬特出一身汗——恰夠誦一句禱詞之時——並將汗珠化為十五歲少年之軀，光明而修長。他一出汗便見世界黑如夜、大地遍生毒蟲；死神阿斯托維達特攜千魔來索，然其壽數未至：對頭降臨之後他又活了三十年，並言：「毀滅者雖來，人類皆出自我之族裔。」

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal text rendered as myth; Gayomart parallels Purusha/Ymir in the dismembered-primordial cluster. No living community restriction.

passages.text: And before his coming to Gayomart, Auharmazd brought forth a sweat upon Gayomart, so long as he might recite a prayer of one stanza; moreover, Auharmazd formed that sweat into the youthful body of a man of fifteen years, radiant and tall. When Gayomart issued from the sweat he saw the world dark as night, and the earth as though not a needle's point remained free from noxious creatures; the celestial sphere was in revolution, and the sun and moon remained in motion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. III, 19-20 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

passages.text: And the evil spirit thought that the creatures of Auharmazd were all rendered useless except Gayomart, and Asto-vidad with a thousand demons, causers of death, were let forth by him on Gayomart. But his appointed time had not come, and he obtained no means of noosing him; as it is said that, when the opposition of the evil spirit came, the period of the life and rule of Gayomart was appointed for thirty years. After the coming of the adversary he lived thirty years, and Gayomart spoke thus: although the destroyer has come, mankind will be all of my race; and this one thing is good, when they perform duty and good works.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. III, 21-23 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

title.en: Mashya and Mashyoi, the First Human Pair
title.zh: 初人夫婦瑪什亞與瑪什雅娜

region.zh: 赫瓦尼拉斯荒野（象徵性定位）

source.work: Bundahishn ch. XV (Pahlavi), trans. E. W. West, SBE 5 (1880)

summary.en: From Gayomart's seed, purified in the sun and guarded by the angel Nerioc-sangh, a rhubarb plant grows, joined to form the first human pair. Auharmazd speaks to Mashya and Mashyoi: you are man, you are the ancestry of the world, perform devotedly the duty of the law, think good thoughts, speak good words, do good deeds, and worship no demons. Their first words acknowledge the creation, but antagonism rushes into their minds and they cry that the evil spirit created the water and earth; by that false speech their souls are in hell until the future existence. They milk a white-haired goat, and the taste of the food is taken away by the demons.
summary.zh: 原人之種經日光淨化，生出大黃狀聖草，相合成初人夫婦。阿胡拉·馬茲達告誡：「你們是人類始祖，當守律法、思善言善行，勿拜群魔！」夫婦初念感恩，然魔意乘虛而入，他們竟呼「水土萬物皆惡靈所造」——因此謊言，其魂直待末日方得救贖。他們以口吮山羊之乳，惡魔遂奪去食物的滋味。

sensitivity.note: Pahlavi doctrinal text rendered as myth; first-pair narrative parallels Adam/Manu. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Auharmazd spoke to Mashya and Mashyoi thus: you are man, you are the ancestry of the world, and you are created perfect in devotion by me; perform devotedly the duty of the law, think good thoughts, speak good words, do good deeds, and worship no demons! Both of them first thought this, that one of them should please the other, as he is a man for him; and the first words spoken by them were these, that Auharmazd created the water and earth, plants and animals, the stars, moon, and sun, and all prosperity whose origin and effect are from the manifestation of righteousness.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XV, 6-7 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

passages.text: And, afterwards, antagonism rushed into their minds, and their minds were thoroughly corrupted, and they exclaimed that the evil spirit created the water and earth, plants and animals, and the other things as aforesaid. That false speech was spoken through the will of the demons, and the evil spirit possessed himself of this first enjoyment from them; through that false speech they both became wicked, and their souls are in hell until the future existence.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XV, 8-9 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.

passages.text: And they had gone thirty days without food, covered with clothing of herbage; and after the thirty days they went forth into the wilderness, came to a white-haired goat, and milked the milk from the udder with their mouths. When they had devoured the milk Mashya said to Mashyoi thus: my delight was owing to it when I had not devoured the milk, and my delight is more delightful now when it is devoured by my vile body. That second false speech enhanced the power of the demons, and the taste of the food was taken away by them, so that out of a hundred parts one part remained.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Bundahishn ch. XV, 10-12 (West, SBE 5, 1880); not verbatim.
